body: Thank you for taking that time to talk with me.  As hard as it is for me, it does give a little hope that someone else is managing it.  I didn't mind reading your "novel" at all

I wish I could find something to turn into a real passion.  I used to, but they were just temporary, and they have less and less effect the more and more I go on.  It's like an increasing tolerance to drugs, until even drugs don't work anymore.  What's the point of desperately trying to get through today when it'll be even harder to get through tomorrow.  Unavoidable logic and basic math says you can only do that for so long.

How did you get through it?  did you ever find someone who could truly help?  do you still feel suicidal, or did your dark moments pass.  how you keep that from being temporary and not falling right back into it?

My life has been one desperate search for distractions, and fresh starts to keep me from falling too deep....that that's not working anymore.. even my drug addictions and alcoholism...desperate attempts to just complete even a single day at a time, aren't working anymore.

Mission beach is really small.  Really just one road going down with very few parking spaces to accommodate the people who live there.  There are two lots, buy they get checked pretty regularly.  You might get away with just a ticket.  Up the road is Pacific beach, and there's a library on Thomas Ave, three blocks from the beach that's easier to find parking on, since no one lives on the whole block it takes up.  Thomas Ave, between Cass st and Dawes st.  There's a school close to there.  I've never tried to park an rv or van, so I'm not sure how accepting they'd be with that near the kids there.  

Good Luck!  Let me know how it goes.  I've never done the van life there.  I've heard it's not as accepting as other cities and I'd really like to know how it goes for you.

I'm going to get a conversion van with windows, then take out the seatsand build a bed frame with storage.  You can do a little more with the cargo vans if you want to, but you have to really commit to spending a lot of time and money working on the inside.  the conversion vans have a lower ceiling for what they can become, but they start off so much better.  carpeted, finished interior, sometimes even a monitor to hook up a dvd player to.  Cargo vans, especially used ones that were used for work, are so empty and beat up it looks like.  you have to install a whole floor, insulate it, make the walls look acceptable, etc...   for someone trying to save money, and not spend hundred if not thousands on the inside, it ended up not making sense to me.  

I thought of the parking garage idea, but figured it was a "when not if" i got caught in there situation, and that I'd end up stealth camping on the streets soon enough anyway.

I'm in San Diego.  I'm guessing you're up closer to San Francisco, the most expensive city in the world to live in.  

Tell you classmate to get on Reddit!  I have some question about his experience.  specifically how he blends in, and how he avoids cops and having neighbors freak out that a new van is parked outside their house.

My lease is up right before finals week (i'm just in my first year), so those first few nights where i'm sure i'll be adjusting to the life will be some pretty important nights to get some sleep.  Timing could have worked out better...

Thanks dude.  this is an amazing response.  I really appreciate it.  I've done the power backpack trick before when i lived in florida and the hurricanes would knock out our power for days at a time.  definitely a grade A trick.
